Solutions 2 M KCl (see Recipes) 5 M NaCl (see Recipes) 3 M NaOAc (see Recipes) 1 M MgCl 2 (see Recipes) 1 M spermidine (see Recipes) 1 M Tris (pH 7.5 at ~20 °C) (see Recipes) 1 M dithiothreitol (DTT) (see Recipes) X-gal (100 μg/mL) in dimethylformamide (see Recipes) 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0 at ~20 °C) (see Recipes) Tris-borate-EDTA (TBE) (10×) (see Recipes) Tris-acetate-EDTA (TAE) (50×) (see Recipes) Transcription buffer (10×) (see Recipes) Selection buffer (10×) (see Recipes) Loading buffer (2×) (see Recipes) Crush-soak buffer (see Recipes)

Add deionized H 2 O to 1 L. Autoclave. 1 M dithiothreitol (DTT) Add 154 mg of DTT to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube. Add 1 mL of dH 2 O. Vortex to mix. X-gal (100 μg/mL) in dimethylformamide Add 100 mg of X-gal to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube. Add 1 mL of dimethylformamide. Vortex to mix. 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0 at ~20 °C) Add 186.1 g of EDTA to a 1 L flask. Add deionized H 2 O to ~800 mL. Stir to mix. Add 15 g of NaOH pellets. Stir to mix. While stirring, adjust pH with 10 N sodium hydroxide to pH 8.

Add deionized H 2 O to 1 L. Autoclave. TBE (10× concentrated, 4 L) To a 4 L flask, add 432 g of Tris base, 220 g of boric acid, 14.9 g of EDTA, and deionized H 2 O to 4 L. Stir to mix. Filter particulates. Sterilize by autoclaving. The final solution is a 10× concentration buffer containing 0.9 M Tris, 0.9 M borate, and 10 mM EDTA pH 8.0 at ~20 °C. TAE (50× concentrated, 1 L) To a 1 L flask, add 242 g of Tris base, deionized H 2 O to ~800 mL, 57.1 mL of glacial acetic acid, and 100 mL of 0.5 M EDTA pH 8.0 at ~20 °C. Add deionized H 2 O to 1 L. Filter particulates. Sterilize by autoclaving. The final solution is a 50× concentrated buffer containing 2 M Tris, 1 M acetate, and 50 mM EDTA pH 8.0 at ~20 °C. Transcription buffer (10× concentrated, 1 mL) Mix 150 μL of 1 M MgCl 2 , 20 μL of 1 M spermidine, 500 μL of 1 M Tris (pH 7.5 at ~20 °C), 50 μL of 1 M DTT, and 280 μL of dH 2 O in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube. 1× mixture: 150 mM MgCl 2 , 20 mM spermidine, 500 mM Tris (pH 7.5 at ~20 °C), and 50 mM DTT. Store at -20 °C Selection buffer (10× concentrated, 100 mL) Mix 4.77 g of HEPES, 50 mL of 2 M KCl, 1 mL of 1 M MgCl 2 , and 35 mL of deionized H 2 O together in a flask containing a magnetic stir bar. Adjust the pH of the solution to 7.4 by adding pre-weighed NaOH pellets while stirring. Once a pH of 7.4 is attained, remove any remaining NaOH pellets with a clean spatula. Dry and weigh the pellets. After calculating the amount of NaOH required to adjust the pH (typically ~70 mM), add a volume (typically ~0.6 mL) of 5 M NaCl to the solution to bring the total [Na + ] to 100 mM. Add deionized H 2 O to adjust the final volume of the solution to 100 mL. Filter-sterilize the resulting solution. The final solution is a 10× concentrated selection buffer containing 200 mM HEPES, 1 M KCl, 30 mM NaCl (total [Na + ]: 100 mM), and 10 mM MgCl 2 , pH 7.4 at ~20 °C [1×: 20 mM HEPES, 100 mM KCl, 3 mM NaCl (total [Na + ]: 10 mM), and 1 mM MgCl 2 ]. HEPES is light-sensitive, so store this buffer in a darkened compartment (cabinet, refrigerator, etc.). Loading buffer (2× concentrated, 40 mL) Add 44 g of urea to a flask and add 28 mL of dH 2 O. Stir with gentle heat until urea is dissolved. Add 8 g of sucrose, 20 mg of bromophenol blue, 20 mg of xylene cyanole FF, 0.4 mL of 10% SDS, and 4 mL of 10× TBE. Stir with gentle heat until sucrose is dissolved. Store at 4 °C. Crush-soak buffer To a 1 L flask, add 40 mL of 5 M NaCl, 10 mL of 1 M Tris (pH 7.5 at ~20 °C), and 2 mL of 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0 at ~20 °C). Add deionized H 2 O to 1 L. Autoclave. steps.title: Prepare 2 M KCl solution
steps.instruction: Add 14.9 g KCl to a 100 mL flask, add deionized H₂O to 100 mL, stir, filter‑sterilize.

steps.title: Prepare 5 M NaCl solution
steps.instruction: Add 29.2 g NaCl to a 100 mL flask, add deionized H₂O to 100 mL, stir, filter‑sterilize.

steps.title: Prepare 3 M NaOAc solution
steps.instruction: Add 24.6 g sodium acetate (NaOAc) to a 100 mL flask, add deionized H₂O to 100 mL, stir, filter‑sterilize.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M MgCl₂ solution
steps.instruction: Add 9.5 g MgCl₂·6H₂O to a 100 mL flask, add deionized H₂O to 100 mL, stir, filter‑sterilize.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M spermidine solution
steps.instruction: Add 145 mg spermidine to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 1 mL dH₂O, vortex, then add another 1 mL sterile dH₂O.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M Tris buffer (pH 7.5)
steps.instruction: Add 121.1 g Tris base to a 1 L flask, add ~900 mL dH₂O while stirring, adjust pH to 7.5 with HCl, bring volume to 1 L with dH₂O, autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M DTT solution
steps.instruction: Add 154 mg DTT to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 1 mL dH₂O, vortex to mix.

steps.title: Prepare X‑gal (100 µg/mL) in DMF
steps.instruction: Add 100 mg X‑gal to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 1 mL dimethylformamide, vortex to mix.

steps.title: Prepare 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0)
steps.instruction: Add 186.1 g EDTA to a 1 L flask, add ~800 mL dH₂O, stir, add 15 g NaOH pellets, stir, adjust pH to 8.0 with 10 N NaOH, bring to 1 L with dH₂O, autoclave.

steps.title: Prepare 10× TBE buffer (4 L)
steps.instruction: To a 4 L flask add 432 g Tris base, 220 g boric acid, 14.9 g EDTA, add dH₂O to 4 L, stir, filter particulates, autoclave (final 10×: 0.9 M Tris, 0.9 M borate, 10 mM EDTA, pH 8.0).

steps.title: Prepare 50× TAE buffer (1 L)
steps.instruction: To a 1 L flask add 242 g Tris base, ~800 mL dH₂O, 57.1 mL glacial acetic acid, 100 mL 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0), bring to 1 L with dH₂O, filter, autoclave (final 50×: 2 M Tris, 1 M acetate, 50 mM EDTA, pH 8.0).

steps.title: Prepare 10× transcription buffer (1 mL)
steps.instruction: Mix in a 1.5 mL tube: 150 µL 1 M MgCl₂, 20 µL 1 M spermidine, 500 µL 1 M Tris (pH 7.5), 50 µL 1 M DTT, 280 µL dH₂O (final 1×: 150 mM MgCl₂, 20 mM spermidine, 500 mM Tris, 50 mM DTT). Store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 10× selection buffer (100 mL)
steps.instruction: In a flask with magnetic stir bar add 4.77 g HEPES, 50 mL 2 M KCl, 1 mL 1 M MgCl₂, and 35 mL dH₂O; adjust pH to 7.4 with pre‑weighed NaOH pellets, remove excess pellets, add ~0.6 mL 5 M NaCl to reach total [Na⁺] = 100 mM, bring volume to 100 mL with dH₂O, filter‑sterilize (final 10×: 200 mM HEPES, 1 M KCl, 30 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl₂, pH 7.4). Store protected from light.

steps.title: Prepare 2× loading buffer (40 mL)
steps.instruction: Add 44 g urea to a flask, add 28 mL dH₂O, stir with gentle heat until dissolved; add 8 g sucrose, 20 mg bromophenol blue, 20 mg xylene cyanole FF, 0.4 mL 10 % SDS, 4 mL 10× TBE, stir with gentle heat until sucrose dissolves; store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare crush‑soak buffer (1 L)
steps.instruction: To a 1 L flask add 40 mL 5 M NaCl, 10 mL 1 M Tris (pH 7.5), 2 mL 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0), add dH₂O to 1 L, autoclave.

steps.title: Design and order oligonucleotides
steps.instruction: Choose a riboswitch scaffold (e.g., Guanine‑I), decide which nucleotides to randomize (≥23 N positions), design a 12–18 nt 3′‑biotinylated capture oligo (optionally with TEG spacer), design forward primer with T7 promoter (TAATACGACTCACTATAGG) plus pool‑specific sequence, design reverse primer as reverse complement of 3′ region, design single‑stranded reverse‑complement DNA template containing ~15 bp overlap with forward primer and N‑randomized region; order all oligos (≥200 nmol for template, standard scale for primers and capture) with standard desalting and PAGE‑purify in‑house or order PAGE‑purified.

steps.title: Generate G0 double‑stranded DNA template
steps.instruction: In a 0.2 mL tube combine 100 pmol reverse‑complement template DNA, 150 pmol forward primer, and dH₂O to 30 µL; heat at 90 °C for 1 min, cool at room temperature for 3 min; add 5 µL 10 mM dNTPs, 10 µL 5× first‑strand buffer, 2.5 µL 0.1 M DTT, 2.5 µL SuperScript III RT; incubate 55 °C for 1 h; heat‑inactivate at 75 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: In‑vitro transcribe G0 RNA pool
steps.instruction: Set up a 0.5 mL tube with: 10 µL 10× transcription buffer, 20 µL 10 mM NTPs, 12.5 µL dsDNA G0 template (~25 pmol), 55 µL dH₂O, 2.5 µL T7 RNA polymerase; incubate 37 °C for 2 h (or until Mg₂P₂O₇ precipitate appears, possibly overnight).

steps.title: Digest DNA template
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL TURBO DNase (2 U/µL) to the transcription reaction, incubate 37 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Prepare denaturing PAGE and load RNA
steps.instruction: Prepare an 8 M urea 10 % polyacrylamide gel using National Diagnostics UreaGel reagents (use wells ~200 µL capacity). Add 101 µL 2× loading buffer to the RNA, load the entire sample in one well (or concentrate RNA first if volume > well capacity). Run gel until xylene cyanol migrates 5–10 cm, then cover gel with plastic wrap.

steps.title: Visualize and excise RNA band
steps.instruction: In a dark room place gel on a TLC silica gel sheet (fluorescence indicator 254 nm), illuminate with short‑wavelength handheld UV lamp; locate dark RNA band, draw a box on the plastic wrap, avoid the top/bottom 20 % of the band, excise with a razor blade, transfer gel piece to a pre‑weighed 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Crush‑soak and precipitate RNA
steps.instruction: Weigh gel piece, crush with a small pestle, add 2× (v/w) crush‑soak buffer (e.g., 0.2 g gel → 0.4 mL buffer), vortex, incubate at room temperature with rotation ≥30 min (or 4 °C); filter through Spin‑X column by centrifugation (~1 min at max speed); estimate filtrate volume, add 0.1 vol 3 M NaOAc and 2.5 vol cold (‑20 °C) 100 % ethanol, optionally incubate at ‑20 °C ≥20 min (or overnight); centrifuge 17,000 × g 15 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant, dry pellet in a speed‑vac 5 min (or air‑dry); resuspend in 50 µL dH₂O; quantify RNA concentration with NanoDrop.

steps.title: Hybridize RNA to capture oligo
steps.instruction: In a 0.5 mL or 1.5 mL tube combine 10 µL 10× selection buffer, x µL RNA pool (100–1,000 pmol for round 1, 1–10 pmol for later rounds), y µL 10 µM capture oligo (10× molar excess over RNA), and dH₂O to 100 µL total; heat at 90 °C for 1 min, cool at room temperature ≥5 min.

steps.title: Prepare streptavidin‑agarose column
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL streptavidin‑agarose to a Micro Bio‑Spin column placed in a 1.5 mL tube; attach a 27 G × ½ needle to a 3 mL syringe, poke needle through the column cap, pull plunger to create vacuum; place cap on column, press plunger to drain storage buffer while beads remain; wash column with 100 µL 1× selection buffer six times (pipette buffer onto resin, then use the air‑pressure device to drain). After six washes transfer column to a fresh 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Bind RNA‑capture complex to column
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the hybridization mixture briefly, apply the entire 100 µL to the prepared column, push through with the air‑pressure device; repeat the binding by re‑applying the eluate two more times (total three passes).

steps.title: Wash column to remove nonspecific RNA
steps.instruction: Wash the column ten times with 100 µL 1× selection buffer (pipette onto resin, let sit 30 s, then drain with the air‑pressure device).

steps.title: Incubate column with ligand candidates
steps.instruction: Prepare ligand solution in 1× selection buffer; perform three 30‑second incubations by adding 100 µL ligand solution onto the column, letting sit 30 s, then draining with the air‑pressure device; combine all ligand eluates.

steps.title: Concentrate selected RNA
steps.instruction: Transfer combined eluates to a Vivaspin 10 kDa MWCO spin column, centrifuge 12,000 × g 15 min at ~20 °C, discard flow‑through; add 300 µL dH₂O, centrifuge again 12,000 × g 15 min at ~20 °C, recover concentrated RNA.

steps.title: Cluster top sequences (bioinformatics)
steps.instruction: Run selfishCluster.py with parameters ‘‑i ‑5 ‑3’ on the sequencing data to generate fasta files for the top‑ranked candidate classes.

steps.title: Identify conserved motifs with CMfinder
steps.instruction: Execute CMfinder (cmfinder‑0.4.1.18/bin/cmfinder04.pl) with options ‘‑skipClustalw ‑combine’ on each class fasta to produce Stockholm (.sto) files of conserved secondary‑structure motifs.

steps.title: Render motifs using R2R
steps.instruction: Run R2R (R2R‑1.0.6/src/r2r) with appropriate weighting flags (e.g., ‘‑GSC‑weighted‑consensus 3 0.97 0.9 0.75 4 0.97 0.9 0.75 0.5 0.1’) and ‘‑disable‑usage‑warning’ to generate PDF drawings of each .sto file; inspect PDFs to locate full‑length RNA motifs.

steps.title: Design disruptive mutations
steps.instruction: From the conserved motifs, pinpoint nucleotides essential for ligand binding and design point mutations that disrupt these contacts while preserving overall scaffold.

steps.title: Biochemical validation of aptamer candidates
steps.instruction: Perform an elution profile (as in the selection steps) using a single aptamer candidate instead of the RNA pool; expect a ligand‑specific increase in signal for a true binder. Optionally conduct in‑line probing, SHAPE, ITC, or SPR using 5′ ³²P‑labeled RNA to confirm binding and structural integrity; compare wild‑type and disruptive mutants.

steps.title: Construct expression plasmid
steps.instruction: Remove the natural aptamer domain and 2–3 bp of the P1 stem from the chosen riboswitch; graft the engineered aptamer (with its primer‑binding regions removed except for 2–3 bp adjacent to the core) onto the natural expression platform; place a common promoter (e.g., thiC for E. coli or lysC for B. subtilis) upstream; clone the construct upstream of a lacZ reporter gene (or GFP/luciferase) in an appropriate plasmid.

steps.title: Transform host cells
steps.instruction: Introduce the plasmid into the model organism that naturally contains the original riboswitch (E. coli strain BW25113 or B. subtilis strain 1A1) by standard transformation or electroporation protocols.

steps.title: Assay riboswitch function in cells
steps.instruction: Grow transformed cells in media containing X‑gal (100 µg/mL); split cultures and supplement one set with the target ligand (e.g., quinine or caffeine) and leave the other without ligand; incubate under appropriate conditions; observe differential blue coloration indicating ON/OFF switching; confirm that disruptive‑mutant constructs show reduced or absent switching.

steps.title: Quantify β‑galactosidase activity (Miller assay)
steps.instruction: Perform the Miller assay on each culture (with and without ligand) in triplicate technical replicates; calculate specific activity; analyze differences with a two‑tailed equal‑variance t‑test as described in Mohsen et al., 2023.
